acceptance: Wizard clustering/distribution choices persist into table_tunings for platforms that support them (tests for Snowflake and Databricks).
The console message matches what was written.
The tests no longer assert the defect.
context: Delivered in merged PR #3407: the wizard reads the selected platform's packaged template and records clustering/distribution/sorting/partitioning only when the platform capability registry applies that layout at execution; otherwise it prints a 'not enabled' warning with the registry reason and records nothing (no false success). Tests now assert persistence (Snowflake, ClickHouse) and refusal (BigQuery, Redshift, Databricks, DuckDB). Behaviour change to confirm: Redshift sort keys are no longer copied from the DuckDB template. Not verified against live platforms.
description:
## Problem
`_read_template_table_tunings` always reads the DuckDB template, which has no clustering or distribution slots. Layout choices made in the wizard are therefore never written to `table_tunings`, yet the console prints "✓ Clustering keys enabled". The fix in bf7997e6c (#2419) did not cover this path. `tests/unit/.../test_tuning_wizard.py:82,188,232` assert that clustering is not enabled, so the tests lock in the defect.

## Change
- Read the template for the selected platform.
- Persist the chosen layouts to `table_tunings`, or refuse with a clear message when the platform has no such slot.
- Fix the tests to assert that the choices persist.
